articles.title: Anthropic Releases Claude 4 with Extended Reasoning and 500K Context Window
articles.summary: Anthropic has unveiled Claude 4, featuring a dramatically expanded 500,000-token context window and a new extended reasoning mode that allows the model to deliberate on complex problems for up to 10 minutes before responding. The model reportedly outperforms competitors on graduate-level math and scientific benchmarks by a significant margin. Anthropic also announced new constitutional AI improvements aimed at reducing subtle sycophancy.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini 2.5 Ultra Achieves Human-Level Performance on MedQA
articles.summary: Google DeepMind announced that Gemini 2.5 Ultra has reached human-level performance on the MedQA medical licensing exam benchmark, scoring above 95% accuracy. The achievement is being hailed as a major step toward AI-assisted clinical decision support. Google has partnered with three major hospital networks to begin limited real-world trials.

articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Agent Platform with Persistent Memory Across Sessions
articles.summary: OpenAI has officially launched its GPT-5-powered Agent Platform, which enables developers to build autonomous agents that maintain persistent memory across unlimited sessions. The platform includes new tool-use APIs supporting browser control, code execution, and third-party integrations. Early enterprise customers including Salesforce and SAP have already deployed agents handling end-to-end business workflows.

articles.title: EU AI Act Enforcement Body Issues First Major Fine to Meta Over Training Data Practices
articles.summary: The newly empowered EU AI Act Enforcement Authority levied a €480 million fine against Meta, citing non-compliance with transparency requirements around the data used to train its Llama series of models. Meta has 60 days to appeal the ruling and must submit a detailed data provenance report within 30 days. The case is being watched closely as a bellwether for how regulators will interpret the Act's provisions on foundation models.

articles.title: Microsoft Research Unveils RAG 2.0 Framework with Dynamic Knowledge Graph Integration
articles.summary: Microsoft Research has published a paper and open-sourced a new retrieval-augmented generation framework dubbed RAG 2.0, which replaces static vector databases with dynamically updated knowledge graphs. The system achieves a 34% reduction in hallucination rates on enterprise document QA benchmarks compared to traditional RAG pipelines. The framework is already being integrated into Microsoft 365 Copilot's backend.

articles.title: xAI's Grok 3.5 Introduces Real-Time Video Understanding and Live Web Grounding
articles.summary: Elon Musk's xAI released Grok 3.5, adding real-time video stream understanding and live web grounding capabilities that allow the model to answer questions about ongoing events with up-to-the-minute context. The model is integrated directly into X's video features, enabling users to get AI commentary on live sports, news broadcasts, and user-generated streams. xAI claims Grok 3.5 processes video at 60 frames per second with sub-second latency.

articles.title: Stanford HAI Report Warns of Cascading Failures in Multi-Agent AI Systems
articles.summary: Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute has released a comprehensive safety report documenting 17 documented instances of cascading failures in production multi-agent AI deployments over the past year. The report highlights how error propagation between loosely coupled agents can lead to large-scale data corruption or unintended financial transactions. Researchers are calling for mandatory circuit-breaker protocols and standardized inter-agent communication auditing.

articles.title: Mistral AI Open-Sources Mistral Edge 3B, a Model Optimized for On-Device Inference
articles.summary: French AI startup Mistral AI has open-sourced Mistral Edge 3B, a 3-billion parameter model specifically optimized for on-device inference on smartphones and edge hardware. The model runs at full speed on 2024-era mobile chips with no quantization quality loss, according to the company's benchmarks. Mistral says the release is intended to advance privacy-preserving AI by enabling sensitive workloads to remain entirely on-device.
